e-5797.problem: Given that $x=2\textrm{i}$ is a solution to the quartic equation $x^4 + 13 x^2 + 36 = 0$, find all of the solutions.
e-5797.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(x) = x^4 + 13 x^2 + 36.$ 

Since $f(x)$ has real coefficients and $x_1=2\text{i}$ is a root of $f(x),$ the complex conjugate 

$$
\overline{x_1}=\overline{2\textrm{i}}=-2\text{i}
$$

must also be a root of $f(x).$

Now, according to the factor theorem, 
$\big(x-2\text{i}\big)\big(x-(-2\text{i})\big)$
is a factor of $f(x).$ Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2\text{i})(x-(-2\text{i})) & =(x-2\text{i})(x+2\text{i}) \\  & =({x}^{2}-(2\text{i})^{2}) \\  & ={x}^{2}+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by $x^2+4$ using long division.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{x}^{2}+9 \\  & {x}^{2}+4\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}+13{x}^{2}+36\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{{x}^{4}+4{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,9{x}^{2}+36 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{9{x}^{2}+36}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $f(x) = (x^2+4)(x^2+9).$

To find the other two roots, we solve $x^2+9 = 0{:}$
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+9 & =0 \\ {x}^{2} & =-9 \\ x & =\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

 Therefore, the roots of our quartic equation are $x=\pm 2\textrm{i}, \, \pm 3 \textrm{i}.$

after.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(x)={x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+18{x}^{2}-122x+377.$ 

Since $f(x)$ has real coefficients and ${x}_{1}=-2-5\text{i}$ is a root of $f(x),$ the complex conjugate 

$$
\overset{―}{{x}_{1}}=\overset{―}{-2-5\text{i}}=-2+5\text{i}
$$

must also be a root of $f(x).$

Now, according to the factor theorem, 
$(x-(-2+5\text{i}))(x-(-2-5\text{i}))$
is a factor of $f(x).$ Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-(-2+5\text{i}))(x-(-2-5\text{i})) & ={x}^{2}-(-2-5\text{i})x-(-2+5\text{i})x+(-2-5\text{i})(-2+5\text{i}) \\  & ={x}^{2}+4x+((-2)^{2}-(5\text{i})^{2}) \\  & ={x}^{2}+4x+29.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the quotient when $f(x)$ is divided by ${x}^{2}+4x+29$ using polynomial division.

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,{x}^{2}-6x+13 \\ {x}^{2}+4x+29 & \,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,{x}^{4}-2{x}^{3}+18{x}^{2}-122x+377\,\,} \\  & \,{{x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}+29{x}^{2}}_{―} \\  & \,-6{x}^{3}-11{x}^{2}-122x \\  & \,\,\,{-6{x}^{3}-24{x}^{2}-174x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,13{x}^{2}+52x+377 \\  & \,\,\,{13{x}^{2}+52x+377}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $f(x)=({x}^{2}+4x+29)({x}^{2}-6x+13).$

To find the other two roots, we solve ${x}^{2}-6x+13=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-6x+13 & =0 \\ ({x}^{2}-6x+9)+13-9 & =0 \\ (x-3)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (x-3)^{2} & =-4 \\ x-3 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ x & =3\pm 2\,\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the remaining solutions to our original equation, apart from $x=-2-5\text{i},$ are
$x=-2+5\,\text{i}$
and
$x=3\pm 2\,\text{i}.$

Question 9

Find all of the solutions to x4−2x3+14x2−8x+40=0 given that x=1+3i is a solution.

a
 x=1±3i,±8i
b
 x=1±3i,±i
c
 x=1±3i,±2i
d
 x=1±3i,±6i
e
 x=1±3i,±4i
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we let f(x)=x4−2x3+14x2−8x+40.

Since f(x) has real coefficients and x1=1+3i is a root of f(x), the complex conjugate

x1―=1+3i―=1−3i

must also be a root of f(x).

Now, according to the factor theorem, (x−(1+3i))(x−(1−3i)) is a factor of f(x). Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

(x−(1+3i))(x−(1−3i))=x2−(1+3i)x−(1−3i)x+(1+3i)(1−3i)=x2−2x+(12−(3i)2)=x2−2x+10.

Next, we find the quotient when f(x) is divided by x2−2x+10 using polynomial division.

x2+4x2−2x+10x4−2x3+14x2−8x+40x4−2x3+10x2―x4−2x34x2−8x+40x4−2x34x2−8x+40―x4−2x3+0x2+8x0

Thus, f(x)=(x2−2x+10)(x2+4).

To find the other two roots, we solve x2+4=0:

x2+4=0x2=−4x=±2i.

Therefore, the roots of our quartic equation are x=1±3i,±2i.

Question 10
?

Find all of the solutions to x4−6x3+10x2−30x+25=0 given that x=5i is a solution.

a
x=±5i,±2
b
x=±5i,2,3
c
x=±5i,2,5
d
x=±5i,±5
e
x=±5i,1,5
Submit

decision.explanation: The conjugate root is -√5 i, giving the factor x^2+5. The polynomial factors as (x^2+5)(x^2-6x+5)=(x^2+5)(x-1)(x-5). Thus all solutions are ±√5 i, 1, and 5.

Question 10
?

Find all of the solutions to x4−6x3+10x2−30x+25=0 given that x=5i is a solution.

a
x=±5i,±2
b
x=±5i,2,3
c
x=±5i,2,5
d
x=±5i,±5
e
x=±5i,1,5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we let f(x)=x4−6x3+10x2−30x+25.

Since f(x) has real coefficients and x1=5i is a root of f(x), the complex conjugate

x1―=5i―=−5i

must also be a root of f(x).

Now, according to the factor theorem, (x−5i)(x−(−5i)) is a factor of f(x). Expanding the parentheses, we obtain (x−5i)(x−(−5i))=(x−5i)(x+5i)=(x2−(5i)2)=x2+5.

Next, we find the quotient when f(x) is divided by x2+5 using long division.

x2−6x+5x2+5x4−6x3+10x2−30x+25x4−6x3+05x2―x4−6x3+05x2−30xx4−6x3−15x2−30x―2x4+205x230x++252x4+205x230x++25―2x4+72x200000000000

Thus, f(x)=(x2+5)(x2−6x+5).

To find the other two roots, we solve x2−6x+5=0: x2−6x+5=0(x−1)(x−5)=0x=1,5.

Therefore, the roots of our quartic equation are x=±5i,1,5.
